ECE 685 | Power Systems Design L18
Three-Phase Transformers II
Three-phase network models, autotransformers, and
taps
Buxin She
Mike Wiegers Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

Lecture outline
1 Build a balanced three-phase model from the single-phase equivalent.
2 A complete bank-rating and impedance example.
3 Autotransformer construction and operating concept.
4 Physical taps, off-nominal ratio, and model conventions.
Establish actual H/L relations, choose compatible bases, then normalize.

Autotransformer applications
Applications Voltage-level interconnection and voltage adjustment.
Material saving Nearby voltage levels give a smaller magnetic power share,
allowing less winding material and a compact unit.
Isolation H and L share an electrical path; there is no galvanic isolation.
System effects Grounding and transferred overvoltages are linked. Lower
impedance can increase short-circuit current.

T ap-changing equipment
De-energized Change tap position with the transformer de-energized. Select a
planned operating ratio.
On-load Change tap position while supplying load. Adjust the ratio during
operation.
Transition path On-load switching maintains the load-current path. A transition
resistor or reactor limits current between adjacent taps.

Summary
1 Choose the model level; retain winding resistance and leakage, and state the
excitation assumption.
2 Use the connection to obtain phase impedance; retain voltage and current
displacement.
3 An autotransformer has shared series/common sections and no H/L galvanic
isolation.
4 An off-nominal tap is the actual ratio divided by the chosen base ratio.
A useful transformer model preserves the physical connection and names every ratio.
